If the launcher exits in the instant after the cancel-deadline liveness check, the caller reports observer 97 with UNRESOLVED text 'still alive at its cancel deadline' while the receipt shows alive_now=false / launcher_start_now=<gone>; its real exit is then only in SUPERVISOR_RECORD.json (never reaped by the caller). Truthful 'unresolved', not a fake exit; the receipt exposes the state.
When the receipt write fails the stdout line still prints `caller receipt=<path>`; the failure is on stderr only (same log under the transport, 2>&1). Cosmetic.

Exit-code overlap: the launcher can itself exit 70/90/91 (runner 90/91 passed through as RUNNER_NONZERO) and the caller uses 70/90/91 for its own pre-spawn/receipt conditions; disambiguation is by the stdout line (`launcher exit=N` present only for a real exit) and the receipt, not by exit code alone. Same class as the driver's finish codes. Readers/grant text should key on the stdout line + receipt.

Run binding uses the oldest lexical match of `VALIDATION-V6-*-<pid>-*`; a stale run directory from an earlier run with the same pid number could misbind (V6B-04 lineage). runs/ does not exist yet, so the first native run cannot misbind; the receipt records the bound path.

HUP is not trapped by the caller (nor by the launcher outside SELF-HOLD — unchanged V6.1, out of scope). Under `setsid -f` there is no controlling terminal; a caller death by HUP/KILL leaves the launcher under its own bounds with no caller receipt, and the transport receipt records the caller's signal death — three artefacts still not conflated. Precondition: transport as Stage 1, never the raw bash tool.
If S4R6_OUTER_S/S4R6_GRACE_S are set in the environment the caller's bound follows them, consistent with the launcher; the grant should state the environment (defaults) explicitly.
